text: A coin in the gravel, worn smooth on one side and sharp as new on the other. The sharp side is not a face you know.

choices.text: Put it back the way it lay

text: An iron nail driven into a birch at exactly your height. Then another, ten paces on. Then another.

choices.text: Turn and walk the other way

text: One bootprint in soft ground, filling slowly with water. Yours are smaller, and there is only the one.
A cairn nobody has weathered yet. The top stone is warm.
A glass net-float in the reeds, the size of a fist, with something dark suspended inside it that does not move when you turn it.
A ring of keys hung on a wall at eye height. Seven of them, and one is much older than the rest.

choices.text: Hang them higher, where they will be seen

text: A storm lantern burning on a doorstep at midday, and the house behind it shut.

speaker: A surveyor
text: A surveyor is packing up a tripod. The ground is off here, they say, without being asked. Only by a little. Only since Tuesday.

choices.text: Ask what was here on Monday

text: A dog walks beside you for two hundred metres, matching your pace exactly, and then stops at a line on the pavement you cannot see.

speaker: A fisher
text: A fisher hauling in far too early. They stopped biting, she says. All of them. At once.

choices.text: Ask what they were biting before

text: A child counting windows aloud. They are at four hundred and nine, and they are not wrong.

choices.text: Count the next one with them
Ask what happens at the end

speaker: A forester
text: A forester marking trees with blue paint. Every tree. Not for felling, he says. For keeping track.
Somebody passes going the other way, and nods. Twenty minutes later they pass you again, going the other way, and nod.

choices.text: Turn and watch where they go

speaker: A shepherd
text: A shepherd counting a flock backwards from forty. She reaches nought while three are still walking.

choices.text: Tell her there are three left
Count them yourself and say nothing

text: Rain is falling on this street and not the next one. The line between them is as straight as a wall.
Bells, somewhere behind the roofs. Thirteen of them, unhurried, and then nothing.

choices.text: Come back at the next hour and count again

text: Every bird stops at once. Not startled, but finished, as though the piece had ended.

choices.text: Stand still until they start again
Make a noise of your own

text: The wind here goes uphill. It has been going uphill for some time.
A patch of air as warm as a doorway, out in the open, with no door.

choices.text: Walk through and out the other side

text: Your footsteps arrive a half-beat late, as though the street were returning them from somewhere further off.
Fog comes off the water in a shape, and holds the shape for longer than fog does.
A street between two buildings you would swear were joined. The sign at the end is blank, and has been repainted blank.

choices.text: Note where it was and move on

text: A steel door set into the rock face, painted the colour of the rock, with no handle on this side.

choices.text: Walk on and do not look back

text: The tree with the split trunk. You passed it eleven minutes ago, and you have not turned.

choices.text: Go back the way you came

text: The water is flat as a table, and the wind is not. Something is holding it.
Concrete steps going down into the ground and stopping, four steps in, at a floor.

choices.text: Go down and stand on the floor

text: Your name in chalk on a wall, in a hand you do not know, beside a date that has not happened.

speaker: A baker
text: A stall is closing and the last of the bread will be thrown out. The baker offers you the lot, or the price of it in coin.
A stone the size of a loaf, and a low wall a hundred metres up the path with a gap exactly its size.
Somebody is looking for a dropped key in the dark, and you have the only light.

choices.text: Hold the light and look with them
Hand it over and walk on

text: The path forks. One way is shorter and you have walked it before. The other is longer and you have not.

speaker: A seller of old maps
text: A seller of old maps unrolls one without being asked. You are looking for something, he says. Everyone who walks like that is.

speaker: A pilgrim
text: Somebody with a pack far too heavy for a day out. I found it, she says, and will not say what. You will know it when the ground changes under you.

choices.text: Ask which way she came from

text: The water gives up one note, deep and flat, and takes it back. A fisher on the bank has heard it before, and points without looking.
